correctness.rationale: An explicit normal-basis computation shows the bracket equations reduce to three minors over k[u]/(u^m), independently of the square class d; this proves full commutation preservation and center q^(m+2). The principal-ideal valuation normal form for triples over the truncated DVR computes centralizers q^(2m+2+2j) and the exact counts. Averaging gives the displayed geometric-series formula. The Jacobson-radical quotients distinguish split and nonsplit members; the Cayley transform (r-1)/(r+1) proves the modular dihedral identification in characteristic p=2m+1. Direct multiplication-table computations corroborate q=3,m=1 exhaustively for both d square classes, and selected higher truncations. No finite test is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The nonsplit Frobenius skew quotient's complete centralizer spectrum already exists, and is expressly not claimed as new. The new, independently established content is a nonisomorphic split quadratic-etale partner with an explicit k-linear map preserving all commuting/noncommuting pairs; it transfers full centralizer strata and realizes the split member as the modular dihedral group algebra when the odd length equals the characteristic. The inspected ring commuting-probability and dihedral-unit-group papers do not state or imply that pair or its exact all-element distribution. General ring-isoclinism literature may provide a broader mechanism; this priority risk is expressly retained.

value.rationale: Commuting graphs and centralizer distributions are natural invariants of finite rings and finite group algebras. The theorem constructs a whole parameterized family of genuinely nonisomorphic algebras that those invariants cannot distinguish, and obtains the exact centralizer spectrum for a natural modular dihedral group ring. The split/nonsplit radical quotient obstruction gives a structural reason for why the counterexample matters; it is not a routine single-instance recomputation of the known nonsplit spectrum.
